svg.text: Stateless hash-based signature: FORS+C, a 6-layer hypertree, WOTS with target-sum encoding. n = 16 B, P = 0.
Keygen precomputes the height-11 top tree into a MAC-protected cache.
Layer 0 is the top of the hypertree (signs the public key); layer 5 is the bottom (signs the FORS key). Verification walks 5 → 0.
FORS tree κ (κ = 0..13) at byte 16 + 176κ: revealed leaf secret s + 10 authentication siblings = 176 B
Layer 1 shown: LE32 counter c + 42 WOTS chain values + h siblings = 676 + 16h B
THE MESSAGE DIGEST PICKS EVERY PATH
N = first 184 bits of H(tw₁₂ ‖ P ‖ ρ ‖ 0¹²⁸ ‖ m)
128-byte HASH input (P = 0, root slot zero) · read little-endian
Admissible iff the last 10 bits are 0 (FORS+C): the signer grinds ρ over a < 2²⁰
randomizer trials (≈ 2¹⁰ expected). The verifier rejects any other N after one hash.
Example below: idx = 6,090,676,180 from a real signature.
u_κ = bits 34 + 10κ … 43 + 10κ: leaf of FORS tree κ (10 bits each)
e_L = leaf index in the layer-L tree (h_L bits: 11 for layer 0, 5 for layers 1–3, 4 for layers 4–5)
τ_L = all idx bits above e_L = which tree of layer L (τ₀ = 0: the cached top tree)
idx is also the FORS instance: 40-bit tree field of the FORS tweaks
34 bits → 2³⁴ bottom leaves for a 2³² signing lifetime
14 trees · height 10 · 1,024 leaves each · the 15th index group is pinned to 0
Drawn with 4 of the 10 levels. Verifier per tree κ:
leaf = Th(tw₉, s) at position u_κ, then 10 folds Th(tw₁₀, left ‖ right) with
the signature siblings (order from the bits of u_κ) → root_κ.
Verifier: 14 × (1 leaf + 10 folds) + 1 roots hash = 155 HASH calls
Signature: 14 × 176 B = 2,464 B. Pinning u₁₄ = 0 removes the 15th opening.
w = 3 bits · 42 chains of 8 positions · digits must sum to 186 · no checksum chains
Enc(M, c) = H(tw₄ ‖ P ‖ M ‖ LE32 c): two 64-bit words, top bits 0,
21 + 21 digits x_i of 3 bits each; valid iff Σ x_i = 186 and c < 2²²
(the signer increments c until valid, ≈ 4,740 tries expected)
Verifier: steps x_i+1 … 7 (Th(tw₁, ·)), Σ(7 − x_i) = 294 − 186 = 108 per layer;
42 endpoints → leaf = Th(tw₂ ‖ P ‖ 42 × 16 B), a 704-byte HASH input
SIX LAYERS FROM THE FORS KEY TO THE PUBLIC KEY
Each layer: M_L + counter c_L → 42 digits → 42 chains → WOTS leaf → h folds → M_(L−1) = root of that XMSS tree
Orange: values carried by the signature. Blue: nodes the verifier recomputes. Real example path (idx = 6,090,676,180); layer 0 has τ₀ = 0.
KEYGEN CACHE: THE TOP TREE IS BUILT ONCE

g.text: keygen builds layer 0 (τ = 0, height 11) once and keeps all 4,094 nodes below the root in a 128 KiB cache, masked and MAC-authenticated.
sign reads its layer-0 authentication path from the cache instead of rebuilding 2,048 WOTS leaves; verify never sees the cache.

svg.text: node (l, j), l = 0..10: byte 32 + 16 · (N_l + j), N_l = Σ_(k<l) 2^(11−k); the root (level 11) is not stored, it is pk
stored = X(l, j) ⊕ mask(l, j), mask(l, j) = Th(tw₁₃(l, j) ‖ P ‖ S): 16 B, a seed derivation like the WOTS / FORS secrets
tag = H(tw₁₄ ‖ P ‖ S ‖ region): the full 256-bit answer; 65,568-byte input = 1,025 blocks. A tampered cache fails the check (forgery chance 2⁻²⁵⁶ per request).

g.text: 1 build the top tree: 2,048 WOTS leaves + 2,047 nodes
2 4,094 masks; write X(l, j) ⊕ mask(l, j)
2 digest, FORS, layers 5…1 built from S
3 layer 0: counter c₀; leaf e₀ chains up to x_i only
layer 0 is checked like any layer:
siblings; a wrong sibling gives a root ≠ pk

svg.text: Th(tw₀(lay, τ, i, e) ‖ P ‖ S)
WOTS: 42 calls per leaf; FORS leaf j:
Th(tw₈(κ, idx, 0, j) ‖ P ‖ S), 1,024 per tree
Signer-side only: the verifier sees revealed secrets and chain values, never the PRF.
WITNESS EXPANSION: MOVE THE SIX COUNTERS TO THE END
expand is a fixed byte permutation (no hashing): W = S = 7,080 B. Every 16-byte item of the witness is 8-aligned, so verify reads each with one LD.
layer L body (42 values + h_L siblings): signature counter + 4 → witness 2,480, 3,328, 4,080, 4,832, 5,584, 6,320
Witness charge ⌈W / 256⌉ = 28 cycles. Verify: 13,371 cycles for every accepting run (constant: digit sum fixed, no loops) + 28 = C = 13,399.
Trees drawn schematically; real example paths and digits.
